title: A stranger demanded my employee discount. I don't work there.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A stranger demanded my employee discount. I don't even work there.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Stay to the end, because the final detail changes everything.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I was buying cereal in a red shirt, which happens to be the exact color of the store uniform.

beats.speaker: karen
beats.text: Excuse me! I need my ten percent off. Right now.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I'm just a customer.

beats.speaker: karen
beats.text: <loud>That is exactly what a lazy employee would say!</loud>

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then the actual manager walked over, and he was also wearing red.

beats.speaker: manager
beats.text: Ma'am, she doesn't work here. I'm the manager. How can I help?

beats.speaker: karen
beats.text: Then why is she dressed like she works here?

beats.speaker: manager
beats.text: Ma'am... I'm wearing the same shirt. Are you saying I don't work here either?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She looked at my shirt. Then his shirt. Then back at my shirt.

beats.speaker: karen
beats.text: Well... can YOU give me the discount, then?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He did. Her coupon was real the whole time. She just never asked an actual employee.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: [laugh] I am never wearing this shirt shopping again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So... was I wrong for laughing the whole way home?
